title: Converting units
summary: Convert metres to centimetres, grams to kilograms and litres to millilitres. The conversion strip helps you.
guide: The conversion strip shows units from biggest to smallest. Between two units it says how many of the smaller unit make one of the bigger unit.
From a big unit to a small unit: multiply. 1 {{term:metre}} = 100 {{term:centimetre}}s, so 3 m = 300 cm.
From a small unit to a big unit: divide. 1000 {{term:gram}}s = 1 {{term:kilogram}}.
Sense-check: is the new unit smaller? Then the number must get bigger.
We measure {{term:area}} in {{term:square-centimetre}}s (cm²) and {{term:square-metre}}s (m²). A square metre is a square with sides of 1 m.

metres-to-cm.title: The classroom door
metres-to-cm.prompt: The classroom door is 3 m 45 cm tall. First estimate: is that more or less than 300 cm? Now write how many centimetres it is.
metres-to-cm.hint: Look at the strip: how many centimetres are in 1 metre? Change 3 m to centimetres first, then add 45.
metres-to-cm.success: Well done! 3 m = 300 cm, and 300 + 45 = 345 cm.
metres-to-cm.why: Why is 3 m 45 cm equal to 345 cm, and not 34 or 3045?
metres-to-cm.model: Each metre is 100 cm, so 3 m = 3 × 100 = 300 cm. There are 45 cm more: 300 + 45 = 345. You get 3045 if you think a metre is 1000 cm.

feedback.thousand: 1 m is not 1000 cm. Look at the strip: what is written between m and cm?
feedback.extra-zero: You wrote one zero too many. 3 m = 300 cm. Now add 45.
feedback.added: You added 3 and 45, but they are in different units. Change 3 m to centimetres first.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. How many centimetres are in 3 m?
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. A centimetre is smaller than a metre, so the number must get bigger.

grams-to-kg.title: A bag of flour
grams-to-kg.prompt: A bag of flour weighs 2500 {{term:gram}}s. How many {{term:kilogram}}s is that? (Use a decimal point, e.g. 1.5.)
grams-to-kg.hint: 1000 g = 1 kg. A kilogram is the bigger unit, so divide: 2500 ÷ 1000.
grams-to-kg.success: Well done! 2500 g = 2.5 kg, two and a half kilograms.
grams-to-kg.why: When we change grams to kilograms, why does the number get smaller?
grams-to-kg.model: A kilogram is a bigger unit. Every 1000 g make 1 kg, so there are fewer kilograms: 2500 ÷ 1000 = 2.5.

feedback.wrong-way: You multiplied. From a small unit to a big unit, divide.
feedback.factor: 1 kg is 1000 g, not 10 or 100. Divide by 1000.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. 2500 g is less than 3 kg.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. 2500 g is more than 2 kg.

juice-glasses.title: How many glasses of juice?
juice-glasses.prompt: Zahra has a 1.5 {{term:litre}} bottle of juice. She pours 250 {{term:millilitre}}s into each glass. How many glasses can she fill?
juice-glasses.hint: First change litres to millilitres: 1 l = 1000 ml. Then see how many 250s fit into it.
juice-glasses.success: Well done! 1.5 l = 1500 ml, and 1500 ÷ 250 = 6 glasses.
juice-glasses.why: Why must you change the litres to millilitres first?
juice-glasses.model: Because the glass is measured in millilitres. We can only divide when both amounts are in the same unit: 1500 ÷ 250 = 6. Four glasses make 1 litre, so 1.5 litres make 6 glasses.

feedback.stopped: 1500 ml is right, but the question asks for the number of glasses. Divide 1500 by 250.
feedback.factor: 1 l is not 100 ml. It is 1000 ml.
feedback.too-big: That is too many glasses. Four glasses make 1 litre.
feedback.too-small: She can fill more glasses than that. Four glasses make 1 litre.

square-metre.title: One square metre
square-metre.prompt: The strip says 1 m = 100 cm. Now think: how many {{term:square-centimetre}}s are in 1 {{term:square-metre}}?
square-metre.hint: Imagine a square with sides of 1 m, which is 100 cm. How many 1 cm squares fit in one row? How many rows are there?
square-metre.success: Well done! 100 rows of 100 squares: 100 × 100 = 10000 cm².
square-metre.model: Area has two dimensions: length and width. Each side of the square is 100 cm, so there are 100 rows with 100 small squares in each. 100 × 100 = 10000.

feedback.length-factor: 100 is just one row, the length. But the square has 100 rows. How many small squares altogether?
feedback.factor: We find the area by multiplying length by width: 100 × 100.
feedback.perimeter: 400 cm is the distance round the square, the perimeter. We want the area.
feedback.separator: Type the number without commas, e.g. 25000.
feedback.too-big: Your number is too big. Think of 100 rows of 100 squares.
feedback.too-small: Your number is too small. Think of 100 rows of 100 squares.
feedback.empty: Write your answer in square centimetres.
